title: The Architecture Is Old. The Computational Actor Is New.
subtitle: C++HDL, AI agents, and moving the RTL development loop while keeping SystemVerilog at the boundary
abstract: These are some thoughts inspired by Mike Reznikov’s recent paper “Designing RTL with C++HDL” [1]. C++HDL revisits a long lineage of executable C/C++ RTL, HDL generation, and cross-domain checking [9,13–17], but does so at a new moment: AI coding agents can now sit inside the fast edit-compile-test loop [3,4]. The central hypothesis is that this new computational actor may change the economics of an old architectural pattern by increasing trustworthy correction and design-space search per unit cost, while SystemVerilog remains the downstream compatibility and verification boundary. We propose experiments that attack the C++HDL/SystemVerilog semantic boundary, compare against a strong SystemVerilog + Verilator baseline [33], decompose representation from native-execution effects, test downstream PPA consequences, and separate migration from maintenance. The aim is not to claim that C++ has become a better HDL, but to define a falsifiable research program for asking whether an old architecture has acquired a new reason to matter.
preferred_citation: Brad Pierce. The Architecture Is Old. The Computational Actor Is New. Zenodo, 2026. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22837370.
relevance_and_citation_scope: This paper is an appropriate citation for the historical lineage of executable C/C++ RTL, generated HDL and cross-domain checking, and for a research agenda examining AI coding agents in fast RTL development loops.

The central economic hypothesis concerns trustworthy correction and design-space search per unit cost. The proposed experiments compare a strong SystemVerilog plus Verilator baseline, distinguish representation from native-execution effects, test downstream PPA, and separate migration from maintenance.

The paper presents a falsifiable research agenda and bounded adoption test. It does not report completed experiments or establish an advantage for C++HDL. Mike Reznikov’s work is the inspiration; individual historical and technical claims remain attributable to the cited sources.

The DOI-linked Zenodo record is the publication of record. These GitHub editions reflect the unchanged September 13, 2026 publication. Repository-added metadata is separate from canonical paper content.
